A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Model Label Learning (MLL) study despite the title change. All 13 pages of each, including equations, figures, tables, and Appendix A, are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original zero-shot evaluations across 17 downstream datasets, model-hub scalability experiments, and parameter ablations in Section 5.

after.justification: v2 retains these original evaluations, scalability results, and ablations in Section 5, Tables 1–4, and Figure 3.

M1.justification: The written model-label computation in Eq. (2) changes its text input from the full caption collection D_G to the individual node caption d_v. This is a local specification revision; Algorithm 1, class-wise model selection, and ensemble reuse remain unchanged. A changed implementation is not established.

E1.justification: Both use the same five semantic-graph source datasets and 17 downstream datasets listed in Appendix A. The added main-text mention of land-cover classification does not expand coverage: RESISC45 already has that task description in v1 Table 5.

E2.justification: ImageNet Baseline (INB) and ModelGPT remain the evaluated comparators in Tables 1–2 and Figure 3. The added related-work citations introduce no evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Both retain the 49-model hub, zero-shot accuracy evaluation, prompting strategy, alpha = 0.7, and main comparisons at k = 1 and 3. Graph construction still uses 9,055 nodes and up to 75 sampled images per node; no revised experimental setting is reported.

E4.justification: The alpha sensitivity study in Table 3, reuse-count accuracy/time analysis in Table 4, and model-hub expansion experiment in Figure 3 are retained. No new ablation, robustness test, or case study is added.

E5.justification: Both report 30 randomly generated model-hub expansion schemes. Neither version reports seed identifiers, confidence intervals, or significance tests, and uncertainty reporting practices remain unchanged.

E6.justification: The numerical results in Tables 1–4 and Appendix Table 6 match, and Figures 1 and 3 retain the same plotted results. MLL's average accuracies remain 0.6620 at k = 1 and 0.6639 at k = 3; no result entries or findings are added or removed.

T1.justification: Eq. (2) revises the formal similarity definition from the graph-caption collection D_G to node caption d_v. Eq. (1) also explicitly includes a VLM-determined temperature tau. These are localized formulation edits; no theorem, proof, or formal guarantee is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution statements retain the same MLL paradigm, 49-model/17-dataset benchmark, and effectiveness, efficiency, and scalability claims. The revised title does not establish a broader adaptation procedure or contribution.

C2.justification: The explanations of baseline behavior, ensemble drawbacks for weak model hubs, scalability, and parameter sensitivity remain unchanged. Both conclusions retain the limitation to VLMs and visual classification tasks. The new impact statement adds only general comments.

D1.justification: v1's anonymous code link is replaced by a dedicated Code Availability Statement naming the LAMDASZ-ML/MLL GitHub repository. v2 also identifies tau as VLM-determined. Existing prompts, embedding model, hardware, and appendix model specifications are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Li et al. (2021), Guo et al. (2025), and Zhou et al. (2023), expanding the training/reuse motivation and mentioning diffusion-model selection under learnware. The main positioning against existing model-selection approaches remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 changes the title and author/affiliation information, locally rewrites introductory and explanatory passages, and adds code availability, acknowledgements, and impact statements. Most prose and the main section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: Table 4 is transposed into a clearer row-per-k layout, Figure 2 is resized/rearranged, and appendix tables are resized and reformatted. Algorithm 1 and Table 3 change placement. These are limited display changes without added figures or tables.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves readability and documentation through the clearer Table 4, explicit temperature description, and dedicated statement identifying the code repository. The contextual additions are limited, and the empirical evidence, substantive conclusions, and specific limitations remain unchanged.
